title: S017 — Propagation delta observability / predictive invalidation frontier
description: Determine whether the authoritative propagateJudgments contains enough information to derive a sound predictive invalidation frontier from a prior judgment state, before running propagation.
result_summary: HOLD. The cross-prefix judgment delta (Jh vs Jh-1 by node id, canonical multi-dimensional) is well-defined, deterministic and small: 0.00-0.71 nodes per intervention - the semantic change is genuinely local, unlike S016's global evaluation footprint. But the best frontier constructible from dependency closure + cycle membership is NOT a sound over-approximation: false negatives 0.03-0.35 per intervention (up to 0.30 unexplained for severEdge). Three distinct concepts confirmed: semantic delta (small), evaluation footprint (global), predictive frontier (between, unsound). No incremental propagation, dirty queues, caches or semantic changes were introduced; no src/ change was needed.

answers.Q1_delta: nodes whose canonical judgment differs from the previous prefix; 0.00-0.71 per intervention
answers.Q2_conforms: mostly, but an unexplained residue remains (up to 0.30 for edge interventions)
answers.Q3_s015_false_negatives: the reference resets Phase A to NEITHER (S016), so its evaluation footprint is global while the semantic delta is local; S015 closure approximated the delta and missed global-reset / node-set changes
answers.Q4_cycle_changes: yes - cycle classification captures 0.01-0.32 nodes per intervention
answers.Q5_frontier_constructible: yes - from previous model + judgment map + intervention + reverse closure + cycle membership
answers.Q6_sound: NO - false negatives on both canons for event/edge operations
answers.Q7_expansion_causes: node-set changes from edge mutations; cycle/unfounded reclassification; the Phase A global reset
answers.Q8_escalation_model: partially - DIRECT -> TRANSITIVE -> CYCLE explains most; a residue is UNEXPLAINED
answers.Q10_engine_needs: previous judgment map; previous node set; cycle membership; reverse-dependency index; a node-set-change signal distinct from dependency propagation

next_experiment: frontier soundness with node-set-aware invalidation - include edge-endpoint changes and authoritative cycle membership; test whether the frontier reaches zero false negatives on the seed canons and synthetic topologies.
limitations: Only the two seed canons + 200-step random histories; no synthetic topologies.
The probe's directDelta includes edge ids but not endpoints, which likely accounts for the severEdge/addEdge false negatives - a harness gap, not patched.
